vulnerability_type: Improper input length validation leading to uncaught exception
summary: The QR handler slices the base45-decoded scan buffer to a 16 byte header length before verifying the buffer is that long, so any QR code decoding to fewer than 16 bytes panics and terminates the vault process.
explanation: DC34_HEADER is a compile-time [u8; 16], so `data[..DC34_HEADER.len()]` is `&data[..16]` on a Vec built from fully attacker-controlled QR content. Rust range slicing panics when the end index exceeds the length. The only length guard in the function sits two lines later at main.rs:626 and is nested inside the comparison that has already panicked; it was written to protect the nonce extraction that follows and was never extended to cover the header comparison.
malicious_actor: proximate stranger with no credentials, able to display a QR code to the victim badge
parameter: QR code payload (optical scan, arriving as IpcString)
trigger_flow: attacker QR code -> camera scanner -> VaultOp::HandleQr -> base45::decode -> data[..DC34_HEADER.len()] slice with no length guard -> panic -> process termination
malicious_input_example: a QR code encoding the two character string "00", which base45-decodes to a single byte
